metadata.title: Nonconvexity of fixed odd-power sum-of-squares cones
metadata.description:
This research note gives a negative answer to the general-dimensional fixed odd-power convexity question recorded by Reznick in Oberwolfach Reports 14/2023 and repeated by Blekherman, Kozhasov and Reznick in 2026. For real nonnegative homogeneous sextics whose cubes are sums of squares, the cone is nonconvex in the explicit finite dimension 3*10^62: disjoint copies of the classical coefficient-1 modified Motzkin seed have SOS cubes, while their finite average does not. For every fixed odd exponent q>=3, some finite dimension n(q) gives nonconvexity. No ternary result, minimal dimension, uniform dimension for all exponents or full classification is claimed. Closedness and the earlier convexity of the union over odd exponents remain consistent.

The proof applies classical SOS separation, product truncated-functional positivity and elementary distinct-index counting. The exact seed, its SOS cube and the standard separation, tensor and collision ingredients are credited to earlier primary sources. An explicit rational order-nine moment functional yields the displayed dimension. The verification archive supplies the standalone manuscript source, all 20 initial minors and 24 exact Schur traces, a Python-standard-library checker with full 220 local LDL positivity/reconstruction, exact cube/moment/sign checks, complete expected output, hash/provenance records, claim scope and a dated priority note. The arbitrary finite tensor argument and the general odd-exponent result are proved analytically, not by constructing an astronomical matrix.

Two independent extensive bounded priority audits identified no exact earlier fixed-power result in the sources inspected. Unavailable historical/final versions, partial reading extents and bibliography/index/talk coverage limits are disclosed. This is not a worldwide-firstness guarantee or certificate of present openness. AI tools were used extensively in derivation, literature comparison, reproduction, writing and adversarial verification. This is an unrefereed preprint without human peer review or a formal proof-assistant certificate.
